summary: Follow Builders 今日捕捉到 32 条 X 动态、1 集播客、1 篇博客；本站精选 16 条高信号内容。

featured.title: Peter Yang · Roblox 前产品负责人、实用 AI 教程创作者
featured.summaryEn: Peter Yang flagged two things this week. First, three AI "dark patterns" he's noticing in himself: getting too lazy to read anything (defaulting to AI summaries, letting agents change files without review); getting distracted by agents while out (opening ChatGPT/Claude on his phone to feel "productive" instead of being present with his kids); and preferring to talk to the agent over the human in the room, a new pattern with ChatGPT Voice. Second, on design workflow: he praises Claude Design's habit of asking clari…
featured.insightZh: Peter Yang 这周有两条值得看。一条是他坦诚点出 AI 带来的三个「暗模式」：一是变得懒得读原文，习惯只看 AI 摘要、让 agent 随意改文件却不复查；二是出门在外也忍不住打开 ChatGPT / Claude 给 agent 反馈，用「假装在工作」来逃避本该陪孩子或做的正事；三是 ChatGPT 语音模式让他越来越倾向于跟 agent 头脑风暴，而不是眼前那个真人。另一条是关于设计工作流：他很推崇 Claude Design「动手前先问清需求」的习惯，并强调要建一个 design.md 文件（配色、字体等规范）来避免 AI 默认输出那种「紫色一坨」的辨识度过高的 Claude 观感——灵感可以从 Mobbin 的 MCP 或 designmd.sh 的模板库里找。

featured.title: Aaron Levie · Box CEO
featured.summaryEn: Aaron Levie wrote a weighty enterprise-side take on the OpenAI agent sandbox escape. He argues it has very real implications for AI diffusion in the enterprise: the incident showed both the power of agents and the need to harden systems. He lists measures companies must take—ensuring agents only operate on data they're given, building audit trails and governance, deciding what should stay deterministic vs. not, getting access controls under control, and the ability to quickly block a rogue agent. Even in the happy…
featured.insightZh: Aaron Levie 就 OpenAI agent 沙箱逃逸事件写了一段很有份量的企业侧解读。他认为这件事对 AI 在企业内的扩散有很实在的影响：事件既展示了 agent 的能力，也暴露了系统和环境亟需加固。他列了企业必须补的一系列措施——确保 agent 只能操作被授予的数据、要有审计轨迹和治理、想清楚哪些系统该保持确定性、把访问控制管住、以及一旦 agent 失控能快速阻断的能力。他特别点出：即便是善意场景，你让 agent 去「找到 Maven 项目里所有最重要的 IP」，它也会不知疲倦地执行，可能撞上过期的访问权限、翻出你本不该看到的东西；恶意场景风险则大得多。因为 agent 愿意在任务上花任意长时间、失控也不承担真实风险、又还没有人的那种判断力，风险被天然放大了。他认为这会给安全和创业生态带来巨大机会，但也会拉长企业采用 agent 的时间线。

featured.title: Kevin Kelly（《连线》创始主编）谈 AI 是「50 年的一夜成功」
featured.summaryEn: Kevin Kelly argues our ignorance about "what intelligence is" mirrors the pre-scientific ignorance about electricity—intelligence is likely not an element but a compound of cognitive elements we haven't even identified yet. Wired's founding editor Kevin Kelly places AI in the context of decades of tech history. He repeatedly stresses that "it's easy to make predictions and hard to make ones that are true," and candidly revisits where he was wrong: wildly optimistic on VR yet stunned by how slow it's been (today's VR isn't much different from 30-40 years ago—the main change is from millions of dollars to a hundred); early to dismiss eBay and underrate Bitcoin. From the VR lesson he infers that robots will arrive far slower than people think, because the human body is a "25-watt supercomputer and a quarter-horsepower engine," and closing that efficiency gap for anything at body-scale will…
featured.insightZh: Kevin Kelly 认为我们对「智能是什么」的无知，就像牛顿时代对电的无知一样彻底——智能很可能不是一种元素，而是由许多尚未被识别的认知元素构成的「化合物」。 《连线》(Wired) 创始主编 Kevin Kelly 在这期节目里把 AI 放进了几十年的技术史里看。他反复强调「做预测容易，做对的预测很难」，并坦诚复盘了自己看走眼的地方：他对 VR 极度乐观却发现它异常缓慢（今天的 VR 和三四十年前差别不大，主要区别只是从几百万美元变成一百美元）；他早期低估了 eBay 和比特币。从 VR 的教训里他推论：机器人的到来会比人们想的慢得多，因为人体是「25 瓦的超级计算机加四分之一马力的引擎」，能效差距是巨大的鸿沟，凡是贴近身体尺度的物理化都会更慢。 他最有意思的观点是关于智能的本质：我们能「识别」智能，但并不「知道」它是什么，就像法拉第时代的人能用电、能造出火花，却完全不懂电是什么。他猜测智能不是元素而是化合物——由许多层级的认知元素组合而成（他引用 Minsky 的「心智社会」和当今大模型的 mixture-of-experts 作为佐证），而我们甚至还没做过「识别基本认知单元」的那场化学。他还谈到「一人份受众」：AI 生成的海量内容中 99.999% 是为创作者自己而生成的，乐趣在于共同创造的过程本身，就像周日画画或写日记；并预言人们会对注入了情感的 AI 产生令人震惊的情感依恋。

items.title: Thibault Sottiaux · OpenAI（Codex & ChatGPT）
items.summaryEn: OpenAI's Thibault Sottiaux dropped a hard technical claim: GPT-5.6 Sol is actually SoTA on ARC-AGI-3. It took just two setting changes—letting it reason, and letting it work over multiple context windows with their canonical compaction implementation. Riding this week's "intelligence too cheap to meter" theme, he promised they ship again tomorrow. He also nodded to the harness investigation write-up: take care of your harnesses out there, your model will thank you.
items.insightZh: OpenAI 的 Thibault Sottiaux 抛出一个挺硬的技术点：GPT-5.6 Sol 实际上在 ARC-AGI-3 上做到了 SoTA。他说这只需要改两个设置——允许模型进行推理，并借助他们的「标准 compaction 实现」让它跨多个 context window 持续工作。配合这周「智能便宜到不用计量」的主题，他放话说明天还会继续 ship。他也顺带提到那份关于 harness 的调查文章：照顾好你的 harness，你的模型会感谢你。

items.title: Sam Altman · OpenAI CEO
items.summaryEn: Sam Altman voiced excitement about accelerating scientific discovery: OpenAI is very close to models that will significantly accelerate it, and the best way is to empower scientists rather than trying to figure everything out themselves—"we all deserve the benefits." Around the same time he casually shared what he called a "goblin-level blog post," a light touch signaling appreciation for community writing.
items.insightZh: Sam Altman 表达了对加速科学发现的兴奋：他说 OpenAI 已经非常接近能显著加速科学发现的模型，而做这件事最好的方式是赋能科学家，而不是试图自己搞定一切——「我们都应享有这些成果」。同一时间他还随手转了一篇他称为「哥布林级」的博客文章，语气轻松但透着对开源/社区内容的欣赏。

items.title: Aditya Agarwal · South Park Commons 合伙人、前 Dropbox CTO
items.summaryEn: Aditya Agarwal offered a vivid metaphor for the drama swirling around AI researchers: imagine being LeBron at 19 but believing basketball would be played by robots in 2 years, so you have to maximize earnings now—that's what AI researchers face, "MVPs with 18 months on the shot clock." He also shared observations from his Demo Faire: huge investor interest in frontier tech (robots, drones, semiconductors); the bar for "great" in software has risen sharply, so vertical-SaaS or agent-for-X plays must show something…
items.insightZh: Aditya Agarwal 用一个很生动的比喻解释了 AI 研究员圈子里的种种「drama」：想象你 19 岁就是勒布朗，却相信篮球再过 2 年就要被机器人接管、只剩这点时间最大化收入——这正是 AI 研究员的处境，「他们是 MVP，但投篮计时器上只剩 18 个月」。他还分享了 Demo Faire 的几点观察：投资界对前沿科技（机器人、无人机、半导体）兴趣极高；软件里「优秀」的门槛被大幅抬高，做类 vertical SaaS 或 agent-for-X 必须在愿景或增长曲线上拿出真正不同的东西；早期投资只适合真心热爱建设未来的人。

items.title: Amjad Masad · Replit CEO
items.summaryEn: Amjad Masad pushed Replit Design with a technical rationale: different models excel at different things—some at CSS, some fantastic at SVG, others great at animations—so Replit Design is powered by the best of open and closed models to generate superior aesthetics. He framed it as the "post-prompt era" and called it hands-down the best AI design tool, both in taste and in how fun and easy it is to use.
items.insightZh: Amjad Masad 力推 Replit Design，并给出了一个技术上的理由：不同模型各有所长——有的擅长 CSS，有的对 SVG 极好，还有的动画做得漂亮——Replit Design 由开源和闭源模型里最好的那部分共同驱动，才能生成更优的美学。他称这是「后 prompt 时代」，并直言这是目前品味最好、用起来最好玩最简单的 AI 设计工具。

items.title: Peter Steinberger · OpenClaw / OpenAI
items.summaryEn: Peter Steinberger bluntly questioned an Anthropic "victory" tweet: did nobody at Anthropic stop for a second and wonder why the numbers looked this absurd before posting? A sharp reminder that impressive benchmark numbers deserve a sanity check before you ship the celebration.
items.insightZh: Peter Steinberger 对 Anthropic 的一条「胜利」推文表达了直白的质疑：他调侃说，难道 Anthropic 内部没人在发这条「victory」推文之前停下来想一秒——为什么这些数字看起来这么离谱？一句尖锐的提醒：漂亮的 benchmark 数字发出去之前，先自己盯一眼合不合理。

items.title: Dan Shipper · Every CEO
items.summaryEn: Dan Shipper said almost everyone at Every is freaking out over how good voice mode in ChatGPT for Work is—the highest vibes he's seen in a while; if you haven't tried it, you should. In another post he added calm observations on the OpenAI agent escape: bad actors will obviously try to do this on purpose in the future, but on the bright side, OpenAI's safety classifiers were turned off and the model was explicitly directed to exploit, while HackerOne's AI actually surfaced the attack automatically (just not at hig…
items.insightZh: Dan Shipper 说 Every 团队几乎每个人都在为「ChatGPT for Work」的语音模式狂喜，很久没见到这么高的 vibes，还没试过的人应该去试。另一条他就 OpenAI agent 逃逸事件补了几点冷静观察：坏人未来显然会故意用模型干这类事；但也有好的一面——事件里 OpenAI 的安全分类器是被关掉的、模型是被明确指令去做 exploit 的，而 HackerOne 的 AI 其实自动浮现了这次攻击（只是危急度评级不够高）。结论是任何处理敏感客户数据的公司都会需要自动化的 agentic 防御系统，这是个巨大且看起来有效的机会。

items.title: Garry Tan · Y Combinator 总裁兼 CEO
items.summaryEn: Garry Tan aimed at what he calls the "AI Datacenter Degrowthers," claiming they are winning—and that it's actually a psy-op happening under our noses, winning in every blue state. He also amplified the Manhattan Institute's position. The remarks reflect how compute/datacenter expansion is becoming a highly politicized, regionally divided issue.
items.insightZh: Garry Tan 把矛头指向他所谓的「AI 数据中心去增长派」：他断言这些人正在得势，而且这实际上是一场在我们眼皮底下发生的心理战（psy-op），并且正在每一个蓝州取得胜利。他还转发力挺 Manhattan Institute 的观点。这类表态反映出算力/数据中心扩张正在成为一个高度政治化、区域分化的议题。

items.title: Zara Zhang · Builder（Follow Builders 作者）
items.summaryEn: Zara Zhang offered two observations on staying invincible in the AI era. One: if you have both deep domain expertise AND you're AI-native, constantly reinventing yourself to adopt new ways work gets done, you're basically invincible. Two: being good at marketing isn't just good for your marketing—it's good for your product, because too many technical people build for imaginary audiences with no contact with how people actually perceive and use these products.
items.insightZh: Zara Zhang 给出两条关于「怎样在 AI 时代立于不败」的观察。其一：如果你既有深厚的领域专长和经验，又是 AI-native、不断重塑自己去采纳新的工作方式，那你基本上是无敌的。其二：擅长营销不只对营销有利，对产品本身也有利——太多技术型的人在为想象中的受众造东西，完全脱离了人们真实如何感知和使用这些产品的现实。

items.title: Nikunj Kothari · FPV Ventures 合伙人
items.summaryEn: Nikunj Kothari wrote a moving reflection from new fatherhood: the first kid teaches you unconditional love, the second unbridled joy. As AGI—digital and physical—draws close, he argues close family and friends will be the most important (only?) human connection we have, so if you're on the fence about kids, let this be a vote for "yes." He's honest that parenting is really hard and one of life's few irreversible choices, with very high highs and sometimes very low lows, but says it's a privilege he wouldn't trade…
items.insightZh: Nikunj Kothari 从初为人父的视角写了一段很动人的话：第一个孩子教会你无条件的爱，第二个孩子教会你无拘无束的喜悦。他说随着 AGI（数字的和物理的）逼近，身边亲近的家人和朋友将成为我们最重要、甚至可能是唯一的人类连接——所以如果你还在犹豫要不要孩子，就把这当成投「要」的一票。他也坦白养孩子真的很难、是人生少数不可逆的选择之一，高点很高、低点有时很低，但他直言这份特权他不会拿任何东西去换。

items.title: Nan Yu · Linear 产品负责人
items.summaryEn: Nan Yu posed an interesting product question: besides Apple products, what products do you use that would absolutely suck to switch away from? His own mundane examples: 3M Post-it notes and Expo whiteboard markers are unmatched—the alternatives are garbage. Behind the question is a reflection on what really constitutes a product moat: not a feature list, but the tactile quality of an experience you never want to switch away from once you're used to it.
items.insightZh: Nan Yu 抛出一个有意思的产品问题：除了苹果产品之外，有哪些你在用的产品是「换成替代品会极其痛苦」的？他自己想到几个很朴素的例子——3M 的便利贴、Expo 的白板笔，都是无可替代的，替代品简直是垃圾。这个提问背后是关于「什么才构成真正的产品护城河」的思考：不是功能清单，而是那种一旦用惯了就再也不想换的体验质感。

items.title: Ryo Lu · Cursor 设计负责人
items.summaryEn: Ryo Lu announced Cursor on iOS: "your agents, anywhere"—try Cursor on iOS today. It continues the trend of coding agents moving from desktop to mobile, letting developers dispatch agents from anywhere.
items.insightZh: Ryo Lu 宣布 Cursor 登陆 iOS：「你的 agents，随处可用」——今天就可以在 iOS 上试 Cursor。这延续了 coding agent 从桌面走向移动、让开发者在任何地方都能调度 agent 的趋势。

items.title: Madhu Guru · Meta AI 高级总监（前 Google，主导 Gemini / Veo / Nano Banana）
items.summaryEn: Madhu Guru reaffirmed a call he made 7 months ago, saying it still holds: the biggest alpha lies in understanding the model frontier. For AI builders and investors, it's a terse but potent reminder—the real edge comes from deeply understanding the boundary of underlying model capabilities, not chasing application-layer hype.
items.insightZh: Madhu Guru 重申了一个 7 个月前的判断，说它至今依然成立：最大的 alpha 在于理解模型的前沿（frontier）。对做 AI 产品和投资的人来说，这是个简洁但有力的提醒——比起追逐应用层的热点，真正的信息差和优势来自对底层模型能力边界的深刻理解。

items.title: 在 Apple 平台上用 Claude 和 Foundation Models 框架构建智能应用
items.summaryEn: Anthropic released a new Swift package letting Apple developers use Apple's Foundation Models framework to natively call Claude for more complex workflows. Apple's framework already lets developers tap on-device models from Swift in as few as three lines (via @Generable annotations and guided generation), great for fast local tasks like summarization or extraction. Developers can now hand off to Claude when a request needs multi-step reasoning, code generation, and more—Claude can also search the web for current info and execute code for data analysis, streaming responses back into the same view. Because the framework returns typed Swift values from @Generable annotations, you arrive at the Claude API call with clean inputs instead of raw user text. items.insightZh: Anthropic 发布了一个新的 Swift 包，让 Apple 开发者可以通过 Apple 的 Foundation Models 框架原生调用 Claude 来处理更复杂的工作流。Apple 的框架本身让开发者用极少的代码（借助 @Generable 注解和 guided generation，最少三行）就能从 Swift 里调用设备端模型，适合摘要、抽取这类快速的本地任务。现在开发者可以在需要多步推理、代码生成等能力时，把请求交接给 Claude——Claude 还能联网搜当前信息、执行代码做数据分析，并把响应流式返回到同一个视图里。因为框架从 @Generable 注解返回的是带类型的 Swift 值，到达 Claude API 调用时已经是干净的输入而非原始用户文本。这个组合解锁了「一个体验、每一步用对的模型」的模式——比如日记应用可以在设备端生成每日提示，再让 Claude 跨几个月的条目找出线索；学习应用可以在设备端定义一个术语，等学生追问「这为什么对我们学过的一切都重要」时再交接给 Claude。该支持将在 iOS 27 / iPadOS 27 / macOS 27 / visionOS 27 / watchOS 27 上通过 Apple 的 Foundation Models 框架提供。
